which.item: If your household income is at or below 138% FPL
which.detail: Covered California: "Californians with incomes at or below 138% of the federal poverty level" are eligible for Medi-Cal, and it is free or low cost.

which.item: If you need insurance and are not eligible for Medi-Cal
which.detail: Covered California is "a private health insurance marketplace where people can get income-based financial help to reduce monthly premiums."

which.item: If your income is above 138% FPL
which.value: Covered California with financial help (if under 400% FPL)
which.detail: The federal premium tax credit covers 100%–400% FPL; the California Premium Subsidy adds state help up to 200% FPL in 2027.

which.item: If you lose Medi-Cal for work-rule non-compliance
which.value: Covered California with no financial help
which.detail: DHCS member notice: "you cannot get financial help to pay for a health plan through Covered California. That means you would have to pay the full cost of new health insurance." The county policy letter says the same: individuals who fail the work rule "will not be eligible for subsidized coverage through Covered California, even if they meet all other Medi-Cal requirements."

ptc.value: Household income must be at least 100% of the FPL
ptc.detail: IRS generally requires household income of at least 100% and not more than 400% of the applicable poverty guideline, subject to stated below-100% special circumstances and other eligibility criteria. Do not use the $15,960 2026 HHS guideline as an automatic 2026 marketplace floor; marketplace plan years use a different FPL reference.

ptc.value: Household income must not be more than 400% of the FPL
ptc.detail: The temporary elimination of the 400% cap applied only to tax years 2021–2025, so the cap is back for 2026 and 2027. If income exceeds 400% FPL you are not allowed a premium tax credit and must repay advance payments.

ptc.value: Not eligible for Medicaid/Medicare/CHIP, no affordable employer plan, all premiums paid by the tax due date
ptc.detail: Also: not claimed as a dependent by another person; Married Filing Separately only with an exception; must file a return with Form 8962 if you received advance payments.

ptc.item: Below 100% FPL: assess Medi-Cal and any special PTC circumstances
ptc.value: Medi-Cal screening; PTC exceptions may apply
ptc.detail: California expansion coverage is a possible route for eligible people, not a guaranteed result. IRS notes special below-100% circumstances; a Medi-Cal work-rule failure can preclude marketplace financial help.

premiums.detail: Premium contribution for the benchmark Silver plan, 2027. Covered California's FPL chart.
Silver 94 plans (100%–150% FPL) have lower deductibles, co-pays and out-of-pocket maximums.

Silver 87 plans. The 2027 California Premium Subsidy is designed to lower the federally-required premiums in this band: the state program "lowers federally-required premiums for individuals between 150 and 200% FPL."
Silver 73 plans. No state help applies above 200% FPL.
Covered California FPL chart, 2027. Above 400% FPL there is no federal premium tax credit and no state subsidy — unsubsidized coverage.

state-subsidy.detail: The 2026 California Premium Subsidy Program was available to enrollees at or below 165% FPL who were also eligible for the federal advanced premium tax credit and applied on the subsidized application. It preserved IRA-level premium subsidies for enrollees up to 150% FPL.

Covered California, July 21, 2026: the Legislature appropriated $300 million from the Health Care Affordability Reserve Fund, up from $190 million. "More than 500,000 Californians are projected to receive a state subsidy in 2027, about 30 percent of all enrollees," and nearly 200,000 can choose from two Silver-tier plans with a $0 premium.

state-subsidy.value: Preserves $0-premium Silver plans up to 150% FPL and lowers premiums from 150% to 200% FPL
state-subsidy.detail: The 2027 program design "preserves IRA-level premium subsidies for the lowest-income Covered California enrollees up to 150 percent FPL and lowers federally-required premiums for individuals between 150 and 200 percent FPL." Eligibility for the state subsidy requires eligibility for the federal APTC and applying on the subsidized application.

state-subsidy.item: Zero income alone does not establish state-premium-subsidy eligibility
state-subsidy.detail: Covered California state help supplements federal APTC for eligible enrollees, with additional plan-year income limits. A person with zero wages may have other income; determine actual household income and why Medi-Cal is unavailable. No automatic free marketplace plan.

dates.value: Current members can renew or switch plans for 2027

dates.detail: "Open enrollment, which is when anyone can sign up for a plan, runs for three months beginning Nov. 1 and ending Jan. 31, 2027."
Outside open enrollment you need a qualifying life event to enroll.
Medi-Cal is not tied to open enrollment.

immigrant-2027.item: Groups that keep financial help in 2027
immigrant-2027.value: Lawful permanent residents (green card holders), Cuban and Haitian entrants, Compact of Free Association migrants
immigrant-2027.detail: Covered California: "Starting in 2027, only certain groups — such as green card holders — will be eligible for financial help to lower their monthly costs."

immigrant-2027.item: Groups that lose financial help in 2027
immigrant-2027.value: Asylum grantees, refugees, trafficking survivors (T visa), Temporary Protected Status, work visa holders, student visa holders
immigrant-2027.detail: Covered California lists these as the major immigrant groups who will no longer receive financial help. This follows H.R. 1. Covered California also notes: "If you have health insurance through Covered California now, you can keep your financial help in 2026."

immigrant-2027.item: What this means for a green card holder
immigrant-2027.value: You keep marketplace financial help in 2027
immigrant-2027.detail: This is a change in the law, not a change in your eligibility. Covered California: "You can still keep your health insurance through Covered California in 2027" — the cost changes for some groups, not for permanent residents.

immigrant-2027.item: Applying does not put your immigration status at risk
immigrant-2027.value: "Applying will not affect your immigration status or your chances of becoming a lawful permanent resident or U.S. citizen."
immigrant-2027.detail: Covered California also advises listing everyone in the household regardless of status, because household size and income drive eligibility for the whole family.

immigrant-2027.item: Public charge note (if you are still seeking a green card or citizenship)
immigrant-2027.detail: Covered California states that a federal rule finalised beginning September 2026 changes how public charge is determined, that getting financial help through Covered California may affect a green card application, and that "Most consumers who are eligible for financial help in 2027 may not be subject to the public charge rule when they apply for admission or a green card," with exceptions for asylum, refugee, U visa, T visa, VAWA and Special Immigrant Juvenile Status applicants. The underlying federal rule text and its applicability to your specific case were not independently reviewed for this site.
immigrant-2027.flag: Partially verified: the statement above is quoted from Covered California (the state marketplace). The underlying federal public-charge rule and its interaction with Medi-Cal enrollment were not checked against the Federal Register or DHS guidance in this session, and how it applies to your own immigration case is fact-specific. Talk to an immigration attorney before making a decision on this point.
